title: Stir Up Waters to Catch Fish
coreMove: Disturb the water just enough to reveal reactions while you stay calmer than the target
sourcePressure: Chapter 39 centers on disturbance as a way of exposing weakness and weakening judgment. The law values controlled agitation because anger, confusion, and emotional turbulence can make people more reactive, more readable, and less composed than calm conditions would. Its limit is that provocation fails when escalation outruns control, becomes cruelty, or destroys the strategic advantage of staying calmer than the other side. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
